items.title: Understanding the Mortality Trends in Patients With Ventricular Arrhythmias and Cardiomyopathy: A 25-Year Retrospective Analysis From 1999-2024.
items.abstract: Ventricular Arrhythmias (VA) associated with Cardiomyopathy (CM) continues to be the major cause of death. However, a national longitudinal study examining mortality trends from these conditions is still lacking. This study assessed mortality trends due to these conditions among U.S. adults aged ≥ 25 years from 1999 to 2024. An observational analysis of U.S. mortalities due to VA in patients with CM (ICD-10 I47.2, I49.0 and I25.5, I42 respectively), was conducted using CDC WONDER. Adjusted Mortality Rates (AAMR) per 100,000 calculated and trends were assessed by calculating Average and Annual Percent Change (AAPC, APC), using joinpoint regression stratified by year, sex, race, and region. From 1999 to 2024, 81,204 VA with CM-related deaths occurred with the overall AAMR declined from 2.54 in 1999 to 1.01 in 2024 (AAPC: -3.55%; p < 0.000001). AAMRs decreased from 1999 to 2007 (APC: -7.93), remained stable till 2022 (APC: -0.66), and dropped by 2024 (APC: -6.87). Men exhibited greater AAMRs (2.42) than women (0.68). Racially, the AAMRs were most pronounced in Non-Hispanic (NH) Blacks (1.97), followed by NH Whites (1.42), whereas Hispanics and NH Others experienced similar AAMRs of 0.97. Geographically, Delaware and the Western regions experienced the highest rates of mortality (2.2 and 1.53, respectively). Urban areas had higher AAMRs than rural settings (1.45 vs. 1.4) CONCLUSION: Although VA-CM mortality has declined over the past two decades, differences by race, sex, and geography remain, underscoring the need for targeted healthcare strategies.
items.journal: Annals of noninvasive electrocardiology : the official journal of the International Society for Holter and Noninvasive Electrocardiology, Inc

items.title: Clustered Regularly Interspaced Short Palindromic Repeats (CRISPR)-Based Genome Editing in Inherited Cardiovascular Diseases: Therapeutic Advances, Emerging Editing Platforms, and Translational Challenges.
items.abstract: Inherited cardiovascular diseases (ICVDs) are a broad category of hereditary disorders resulting from pathogenic mutations that alter cardiac anatomy, electrical conduction, and metabolic pathways. The main types include hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM), dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM), cardiac channelopathies, and familial hypercholesterolemia (FH) and are associated with heart failure, malignant arrhythmias, and sudden cardiac death, particularly in young people. Current treatments, such as pharmacological therapies, implantable cardioverter-defibrillators, and heart transplantation, have significantly improved outcomes; however, these treatments are mainly targeted toward symptom control and the prevention of complications without correcting the underlying genetic defects. Recent advancements in genome editing have transformed precision cardiovascular care, with clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats (CRISPR)-based technologies emerging as potential methods for targeting and modifying disease-causing variants. Emerging platforms, such as base editing, prime editing, and epigenome editing, have widened the therapeutic potential of genome engineering by enhancing editing precision and reducing some of the constraints of the traditional CRISPR-Cas9 strategy. In the setting of inherited cardiovascular disorders, promising early results have been obtained in preclinical studies using human induced pluripotent stem cell and animal models, including correction of MYBPC3 and MYH7 mutations in HCM; targeting of TTN -, RBM2 0-, and LMNA -associated mechanisms in DCM; restoration of ion channel function in inherited arrhythmia syndromes; and modulation of lipid-related genes such as PCSK9 , LDLR , and ANGPTL3 in FH. However, major challenges remain, including off-target effects, effective delivery to cardiac tissues, immunological responses, interpretation of genetic variants, and ethical concerns. This review provides a translational, integrated view of the evolution of CRISPR-based genome editing technologies, their application to ICVDs, current preclinical and clinical advances, and the challenges that need to be addressed to achieve safe and effective translation into cardiovascular therapeutics.

items.title: Recurrent Cardiac Tamponade Following an Open Mitral Valve Replacement.
items.abstract: Cardiac tamponade is a life-threatening complication characterized by the accumulation of fluid or blood within the pericardial sac surrounding the heart, leading to increased intra-pericardial pressure and impaired ventricular filling. This is a known complication of cardiothoracic procedures, including coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) and mitral valve repairs, and can rapidly progress to decreased cardiac output, hypotension, and eventual cardiac collapse. We report the case of a 62-year-old male with an unremarkable past medical history who was admitted to the hospital due to recurrent fevers and bacterial infections, which were found to be due to mitral valve vegetation, and subsequently underwent open mitral valve replacement. His postoperative course was complicated by recurrent cardiac tamponade requiring multiple operative interventions, ultimately resulting in an extended ICU stay, but he was eventually discharged to inpatient rehab two weeks after the fact. The recurrent hemopericardium in this case was most consistent with surgical and coagulopathic bleeding, with a possible secondary contribution from an upregulated inflammatory response related to the patient's infective endocarditis. After any cardiac surgery, a high index of suspicion for cardiac tamponade should be maintained in patients who become hemodynamically unstable. Presentation is often nonspecific, and diagnosis requires a high index of suspicion combined with prompt imaging, with the aid of interdisciplinary collaboration in order to successfully treat patients expeditiously.

items.title: An urgent call for quality measures for cardiac implantable electronic device infections in the United States.
items.abstract: Infection is a significant cause of morbidity and mortality among patients with cardiac implantable electronic devices (CIEDs). Over 400,000 CIEDs are placed annually in the United States with an infection rate of approximately 1-2% in the first 12 months after implantation. In 2010, the American Heart Association provided a class I recommendation for complete system removal in all cases of endovascular CIED-I or pocket infection. Retrospective studies have shown that CIED removal is associated with improved outcomes, and prompt CIED removal within 7 days of confirmed infection is associated with lower mortality at 1-year compared to extraction after 7 days. Despite these strong recommendations and existing evidence, data demonstrates that ∼80% of patients with CIED-I do not undergo device extraction. To address this gap, we advocate for creation of an electronic clinical quality measure (eCQM) that would create incentives for hospitals to provide efficient, guideline-concordant care, analogous to existing eCQMs for other conditions, such as ST elevation myocardial infarctions. At present, patients with CIED-Is are dying unnecessarily due to non-adherence with evidence-based, guideline recommended care. Healthcare providers and professional societies, working alongside government agencies, have an opportunity to significantly improve outcomes by developing a sustainable, accountable care model for CIED-Is.
items.journal: American heart journal plus : cardiology research and practice

items.title: Clinical practice guidelines: management of non-post-operative supra-ventricular tachycardia in neonates and children less than 18 years old hospitalized in a Pediatric Intensive Care Unit.
items.abstract: We present guidelines in the form of pragmatic recommendations for management of neonates and children less than 18 years old presenting with non-post-operative supraventricular tachycardia (SVT) and hospitalized in a Paediatric Intensive Care Unit (PICU). Thirteen French-speaking experts, all of them members of the Groupe Francophone de Réanimation et Urgence Pédiatriques (French-speaking group of paediatric intensive and emergency care; GFRUP), collaborated from 2024 to 2025 through teleconferences and face-to-face meetings. The guidelines cover four areas: (1) epidemiology and criteria for admission to a PICU, (2) paraclinical assessment, (3) non-specific rhythm management, and (4) specific rhythm management. The questions were formulated in the Patient-Intervention-Comparison-Outcome (PICO) format. An extensive Anglophone and Francophone literature search indexed in the MEDLINE database via PubMed, Cochrane and Embase was performed using pre-established keywords. The texts were analyzed and classified according to the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) methodology. When this method was not applicable, an expert opinion was given. Each of the recommendations was voted on by all the experts according to the Delphi methodology. The group proposes 21 recommendations. The GRADE methodology could be applied for five of them, and an expert opinion was given for the remaining 16. All of the recommendations received strong approval. These guidelines cover different aspects in the management of non-post-operative SVT in children hospitalized in PICUs including non-specific and specific rhythm management.
authors: French Speaking Group for Pediatric Intensive and Emergency Care

items.title: Photo-induced electron pumping meets nanozyme cascade: Triggering multimodal cell death for potent triple-negative breast cancer immunotherapy.
items.abstract: Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) treatment is often hindered by tumor hypoxia, cellular survival compensation, and the immuno-suppressive micro-environment. Through the "molecular-electron pumping" strategy, a cyanine photosensitizer BrCy5 with excellent Type I ROS generation ability (two kinds of Type I ROS production of BrCy5 are 308% and 206% higher) was developed to realize photodynamic therapy-mediated immunotherapy under tumor hypoxia. In the work, a multifunctional nanoenzyme HMB loaded with Type I photosensitizer was further designed, which precisely delivers BrCy5 and Fe 3+ to tumor cell mitochondria via tumor targeting and lysosomal endocytosis, triggering a lethal cascade of multimodal cell death. Released Fe 3+ catalyzes endogenous H 2 O 2 into O 2 , relieving hypoxia to enhance photodynamic efficacy while depleting glutathione (GSH). Free BrCy5 accumulates in mitochondria, inducing severe mitochondrial dysfunction and lipid peroxidation via efficient ROS generation. This synergistic oxidative stress triggers ferroptosis, activates the Caspase-3/GSDME signaling axis for pyroptosis, leading to massive release of damage-associated molecular patterns (DAMPs) and potent immunogenic cell death (ICD). To enhance this cascade, System Xc - inhibitor sulfasalazine (SSZ) was combined to further deepen GSH depletion and exacerbate ferroptosis. In bilateral tumor-bearing mice, this enhanced regimen created a highly inflamed microenvironment, promoting dendritic cells (DCs) maturation and cytotoxic T lymphocytes (CTLs) infiltration, reversing immunosuppression. Ultimately, it inhibited primary and distant tumor growth, converting "cold" to "hot" breast cancer, proposing a transformative strategy for efficient TNBC treatment by combining the "molecular-electron pumping" photosensitizer, multifunctional nanoenzyme carrier, and metabolic pathway blocking to induce multimodal tumor cell death-induced immunotherapy.

items.title: The EULAR points to consider regarding the development of criteria for the assessment of the disease activity in adult-onset Still's disease.
items.abstract: This study aims to formulate European Alliance of Associations for Rheumatology (EULAR) points to consider (PtCs) regarding the development of criteria for the assessment of the disease activity in adult-onset Still's disease (AOSD). The Task Force consisted of 23 members from 7 different European countries. A systematic literature review and a 3-round Delphi exercise involving European Experts were conducted to support the formulation of overarching principles and PtCs. Based on retrieved evidence and Experts' opinions, results of Delphi Rounds, and discussions, 3 overarching principles and 11 PtCs were developed. The Task Force agreed on the importance of an appropriate definition for the disease activity in AOSD to be valid, reliable, and easily transferable in a clinical setting. The development of specific criteria for the assessment of disease activity should include a precise definition of the clinical features that could better describe the patient condition. A clear definition of disease activity would help clinicians to adjust therapy and to identify refractory patients. A validated assessment of the disease activity is important to establish specifically designed and powered studies for comprehensive management of patients with AOSD. A uniform and reproducible definition of remission may facilitate the inclusion of a new therapeutic target into daily practice and clinical trials. The EULAR PtCs were produced regarding the development of criteria for the assessment of the disease activity in AOSD, to provide the basis for a clinical tool to be readily, reliably, and easily applied in clinical settings in order to improve patient management.

items.title: Drug Delivery Systems for Hepatocellular Carcinoma: Bridging Pathophysiological Barriers and Advanced Nanomedicine Strategies.
items.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is characterized by high heterogeneity, a complex tumor microenvironment, and multiple physiological barriers that limit conventional therapies and cause significant toxicity. Drug delivery systems (DDS), particularly nanoscale delivery systems, offer promising opportunities to overcome these obstacles through passive targeting, active targeting, and stimuli-responsive drug release. Nevertheless, despite substantial progress in preclinical research, the clinical translation of most DDS remains challenging. This review systematically outlines the pathophysiological rationale underpinning DDS design for HCC, including the aberrant vasculature, hypoxia, low pH, overexpressed enzymes and immunosuppressive features of the TME, as well as liver-specific barriers. Subsequently, we comprehensively evaluate the progress and limitations of passive targeting, active targeting, stimuli-responsive, and locoregional delivery systems. Furthermore, we dissect the core bottlenecks currently impeding clinical translation: tumor heterogeneity, the "interlocking chain" effect of multiple biological barriers, uncertainty of the EPR effect, multidrug resistance mechanisms, poorly defined long-term safety of nanocarriers, and the "valley of death" caused by discrepancies between preclinical models and human disease. Finally, we envision future directions: next-generation targeting strategies should focus on CSCs and metastasis; DDS must be deeply integrated with immunotherapy to remodel the immune microenvironment; biomimetic and bio-derived delivery systems may circumvent inherent limitations of synthetic carriers; multifunctional theranostic platforms enable real-time monitoring and personalized treatment; and establishing more clinically relevant animal models alongside personalized DDS design paradigms is key to accelerating translation. Our central argument is that the future success of DDS for HCC will no longer rely on the "showmanship" of individual technologies, but rather on a "systems engineering" approach grounded in a profound understanding of HCC biological heterogeneity, with the core objectives being precise spatiotemporal control of drug distribution and beneficial interactions with the host immune system.

items.title: Immune shifts in inflammatory skin diseases.
items.abstract: Inflammatory skin diseases are driven by dominant immune programs, including T helper (Th)1, Th2, Th17, type I IFN, and neutrophilic pathways, which shape responsiveness to targeted immunotherapies. Molecular profiling has revealed that these diseases frequently harbor additional, coexisting immune programs and that dominance among pathways can shift over time, either spontaneously or in response to therapy. Such immune shifts, which limit therapeutic effectiveness, often occur in the absence of clinically evident morphological changes. In this review, we describe the molecular immune landscape of inflammatory skin diseases, with an emphasis on psoriasis and atopic dermatitis, and illustrate the immune shifts that underlie therapy-resistant disease states and paradoxical reactions. We propose a model of an immune continuum governed by a dynamic equilibrium among inflammatory pathways that is susceptible to displacement. Finally, we highlight molecular immune profiling as a critical tool for detecting such shifts and enabling rational therapeutic adaptation.
items.journal: JID innovations : skin science from molecules to population health

items.title: Survival after lymph node dissection, radiotherapy, and combined treatment in sentinel node-positive stage IIIA Merkel cell carcinoma: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
items.abstract: Merkel cell carcinoma (MCC) has a high risk of regional lymphatic metastasis. In cases of lymphatic micrometastasis, an evidence-based clinical approach is missing. To assess survival outcomes following complete lymph node dissection (CLND), radiation (RTX), or CLND plus RTX (CLND + RTX) in patients with stage IIIA MCC. A systematic search was conducted in MEDLINE, Embase, and the Cochrane Library. Pooled survival rates were calculated using random-effects models. Comparative effectiveness of interventions was assessed via network meta-analysis. Eight studies, including 1825 patients, were analyzed. Pooled 1- and 3-year survival rates (overall survival and MCC-specific survival) following CLND (regardless of RTX) were 93% (95% CI, 89%-96%) and 71% (95% CI, 64%-77%), showing no significant difference compared with patients without CLND. Furthermore, relative risk ratios comparing RTX (regardless of CLND status) with no RTX demonstrated no significant differences for overall survival at either 1 or 3 years. Finally, a network meta-analysis also did not show superiority among CLND only, RTX only, and CLND + RTX in patients with stage IIIA MCC. The limited number of observational studies, data heterogeneity, missing data regarding immunotherapies, and low evidence levels according to the GRADE restrict definitive conclusions. Findings underscore the need for large, prospective clinical trials to define optimal treatment strategies for patients with stage IIIA MCC. CRD42025636348.

items.title: GPR82-mediated activation of TGF-β/SMAD signaling contributes to CD8 + T cell dysfunction in HBV-ACLF.
items.abstract: Patients with acute-on-chronic liver failure (ACLF) have severe CD8 + T cell dysfunction. This study examined G protein-coupled receptor 82 (GPR82) in CD8 + T cell exhaustion in hepatitis B virus-related acute-on-chronic liver failure (HBV-ACLF). Using GEO analysis, clinical samples, GPR82 manipulation, transforming growth factor beta (TGF-β)/SMAD intervention, dual-luciferase assays, and a mouse hepatitis virus strain 3 (MHV-3) mouse model, we found GPR82 overexpression in ACLF liver and HBV-ACLF CD8 + T cells, correlating with T cell exhaustion. GPR82 knockdown enhanced CD8 + T cell function, while overexpression had opposite effects. Mechanistically, lysophosphatidylcholine (LysoPC) upregulated GPR82 transcription via TGF-β/SMAD1, and elevated GPR82 further activated TGF-β/SMAD, forming a positive feedback loop. In vivo , GPR82 knockdown partially restored CD8 + T cell function and alleviated liver injury in the MHV-3 mouse model. These findings indicate GPR82 promotes CD8 + T cell exhaustion via TGF-β/SMAD, and the LysoPC-GPR82 loop offers insight into ACLF immune dysfunction, suggesting GPR82 as a potential biomarker and therapeutic target.

items.title: Presumed hepatic pseudolipoma detected as a small hepatic surface lesion: multimodality imaging findings.
items.abstract: Hepatic pseudolipomas are uncommon benign lesions located on or near the liver capsule which are thought to arise from a detached epiploic appendage that becomes trapped near Glisson's capsule. Because these lesions may appear as small hepatic or perihepatic nodules, they can mimic primary or metastatic hepatic tumors on screening imaging. Here, we report the case of a 55-year-old asymptomatic man with no relevant medical history who was referred after routine health-screening ultrasonography revealed a 10 × 8-mm hyperechoic lesion adjacent to the surface of liver segment VI. Liver function tests were normal, hepatitis B and C viral markers were negative, and tumor markers, including carcinoembryonic antigen, carbohydrate antigen 19-9, alpha-fetoprotein, and protein induced by vitamin K absence or antagonist-II, were within the normal ranges. Dynamic ultrasonography demonstrated that the lesion was located along the hepatic capsule, rather than within the deep hepatic parenchyma. Computed tomography showed a well-demarcated hepatic surface lesion with central calcification and surrounding fat attenuation, without any arterial, portal venous, or delayed enhancement. Gadoxetate disodium-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging revealed fat-containing signal characteristics, no hepatobiliary-phase uptake, and no diffusion restriction. The integrated multimodal imaging findings supported a diagnosis of presumed hepatic pseudolipoma, likely originating from a detached epiploic appendage. Recognition of this benign hepatic tumor mimic may help to avoid unnecessary biopsy or surgery.

items.title: Wesselsbron virus at the livestock-human interface: A practical guide to disease recognition and diagnosis.
items.abstract: Wesselsbron virus (WSLV) is a mosquito-borne Orthoflavivirus of the yellow fever virus (YFV) serocomplex, widely distributed across sub-Saharan Africa. It is neglected, and its true impact is likely underestimated. WSLV causes abortion, congenital malformations, and neonatal mortality in sheep, the primary recognized vertebrate host, but infections have also been documented in goats, cattle, camels, wildlife, and humans. The virus is maintained in complex cycles predominantly involving Aedes mosquitoes and incompletely defined domestic and wild vertebrate hosts. Direct infection via the placenta, milk, and accidental laboratory exposure have been documented. These non-vector routes coincide with routine husbandry in African pastoral and agropastoral systems, creating opportunities for exposure at the livestock-human interface. Severe clinical disease is best characterized in sheep, in which hepatitis, congenital abnormalities, abortion, and neonatal mortality predominate. Similar symptomatology was reported in camels, but causality has not yet been experimentally demonstrated. Human infections are sporadic, usually self-limiting, it can involve hepatic disease, and rarely neurological manifestations. Clinical diagnosis of Wesselsbron disease is challenging because symptoms and environmental circumstances overlap closely with Rift Valley fever. While there is no serological cross-reactivity between WSLV and RVFV, WSLV antibodies broadly cross-react with other viruses of the YFV serocomplex. Molecular assays have improved detection of acute infections, and recent experimental studies have clarified pathogenesis, transmission, and immune responses. This review provides a practical framework for recognizing WSLV infection, selecting appropriate diagnostic samples and assays, and deciding when WSLV should enter the differential diagnosis of Rift Valley fever-like disease in humans, ruminants, and camels. We highlight non-vector zoonotic transmission, improved surveillance, routine diagnostic inclusion, and targeted research to better define Wesselsbron disease in a One Health context.

items.title: Structural characterization of HCoV-229E and H163A main protease (M pro ) interactions with the inhibitor narlaprevir.
items.abstract: Narlaprevir, originally developed as a clinical-stage inhibitor of the hepatitis C virus (HCV) NS3/4A protease, has recently demonstrated potent inhibitory activity against the SARS-CoV-2 main protease (M pro ), with its co-crystal structure already resolved. To elucidate the mechanistic basis of its cross-genus inhibition and drug resistance profiles, we determined the crystal structures of narlaprevir in complex with HCoV-229E M pro and the SARS-CoV-2 M pro (H163A) mutant at resolutions of 2.01 Å and 2.14 Å, respectively. By integrating these crystallographic data with molecular dynamics (MD) simulations and Molecular Mechanics/Poisson-Boltzmann Surface Area (MM/PBSA) free energy calculations, we systematically compared narlaprevir against clinically approved antivirals, including bofutrelvir, PF-07304814, and pomotrelvir. Structural analysis revealed that narlaprevir forms a conserved covalent C-S bond with the catalytic cysteine residue across all investigated complexes. Thermodynamic evaluations indicated that the SARS-CoV-2 WT-M pro -narlaprevir complex exhibits the most negative total binding free energy (-66.29 kcal/mol), suggesting a marginally stronger theoretical binding affinity compared to the 229E-narlaprevir (-64.91 kcal/mol) and H163A-narlaprevir (-64.14 kcal/mol) complexes. Notably, distinct from the approved drugs, narlaprevir exclusively occupies protomer A when bound to both HCoV-229E and H163A M pro . Collectively, these findings establish narlaprevir as a highly promising lead compound with notable broad-spectrum potential. While its overall efficacy parallels that of clinically approved agents, it exhibits distinct binding characteristics. These insights provide a critical structural foundation for the rational design of next-generation antiviral strategies capable of mitigating threats from both circulating and emerging coronaviruses.

items.title: Validation of Baveno VII Criteria using Liver and Splenic Elastography for Predicting Esophageal Varices Severity in Chronic Liver Disease: A Multiparametric, Observational Study.
items.abstract: Baveno VII criteria prioritize Liver Stiffness Measurement (LSM) for portal hypertension risk stratification, primarily using transient elastography. We aimed to evaluate two-dimensional-shear wave elastography (2D-SWE) cutoffs, assess the etiology-dependent utility of spleen stiffness (SSM), and introduce a novel Combined Hepato-splenic Stiffness Index (CHSSI). This ambispective, observational study enrolled 100 chronic liver disease patients. Participants underwent 2D-SWE for LSM and SSM, alongside endoscopy as the reference standard. A novel multiparametric index, CHSSI, was formulated. Diagnostic accuracy for Varices Needing Treatment (VNT; Grade >= II) was assessed using area under the receiver operating characteristic (AUROC). The cohort was predominantly Alcohol-related Liver Disease (ALD, 49%) and Viral Hepatitis (30%). LSM independently predicted VNT (P < 0.001), with an optimal 2D-SWE cutoff of 19.2 kPa (sensitivity 90% and specificity 82%). SSM utility diverged by etiology: it correlated significantly with variceal grade in ALD (r = 0.549, P < 0.001) but poorly in viral cirrhosis (r = 0.174, P = 0.358). The novel CHSSI demonstrated excellent diagnostic performance (AUROC 0.892) for predicting VNT. Liver stiffness remains the most robust single-parameter surrogate for esophageal varices. However, in heterogeneous cohorts where splenic stiffness alone yields inconsistent results, novel composite indices such as CHSSI and Liver Size-stiffness Index offer superior discriminative ability. These findings support a refined noninvasive risk stratification strategy, potentially reducing unnecessary screening endoscopies. Résumé Contexte et objectifs: Les critères de Baveno VII privilégient la mesure de la rigidité hépatique (LSM) pour la stratification du risque d’hypertension portale. Nous avons cherché à évaluer les seuils d’élastographie (2D-SWE) et à introduire un indice combiné (CHSSI). Matériels et méthodes: Cette étude observationnelle a recruté 100 patients. La précision diagnostique pour les varices nécessitant un traitement (Grade ≥ II) a été évaluée. Résultats: La LSM a prédit de manière indépendante les varices (P Conclusions: La rigidité hépatique reste le substitut le plus robuste. Les indices composites offrent une capacité discriminative supérieure.

items.title: Contribution of short-term changes in a composite health score on pathways linking social disadvantage and health: evidence from the UK biobank prospective cohort study.
items.abstract: Chronic and repeated exposure to external stresses may be embodied and generate an adverse biological response, in-turn affecting health. We investigated the role of 4-year change in a Biological Health Score (BHS) in the pathway linking social exposures to all-cause mortality, atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (AS-CVD), and cancer incidence. In this prospective cohort study, we analysed 20,048 participants (10,266 women and 9782 men, aged 37-73 years at baseline) from the UK Biobank prospective cohort with repeated biomarker assessments. The BHS was derived from 15 biomarkers covering cardiovascular, metabolic, inflammatory, liver, and renal systems. We examined associations between BHS change and six social exposures using sex-stratified linear models. Associations between BHS change and subsequent all-cause mortality, AS-CVD incidence, and cancer incidence (ascertained through registry linkage until December 2022) were estimated using sex-specific Cox proportional hazards models adjusted for baseline BHS and time between assessments, with sequential adjustment for additional exposures. Finally, we assessed whether BHS change mediated associations between social exposures and health outcomes using counterfactual mediation analysis. Total BHS increased over a mean interval of 4.3 years in both men and women, as did all sub-scores except the cardiovascular one. Lower education, low qualification, and financial difficulties were associated with greater increases in BHS. A 1-unit increase in BHS change was associated with: higher all-cause mortality in both men (hazard ratio [HR] 1.46, 95% CI 1.25-1.71) and women (1.26, 1.02-1.56); higher AS-CVD incidence in men (1.33, 1.13-1.57) and women (1.24, 1.03-1.48) and higher cancer incidence in men (1.16, 1.01-1.41) and women (1.29, 1.06-1.58). While no clear mediation by BHS change was observed for women, AS-CVD, or cancer, BHS change explained a small but statistically significant proportion of the association between low income and financial difficulties and mortality, in men. Whilst acknowledging the limitations of our dataset, we show that changes in a composite biological score over a few years, independent of age and baseline score, are socially-patterned and associated with subsequent mortality and cardiovascular disease, suggesting that repeated biological measurements may provide complementary information beyond single time-point assessments. Future research should extend these analyses to multiple repeated measurements, enabling the exploration of the dynamics of the embodiment of time-resolved external stresses and their effects on health. Research Council of Norway, European Commission.

items.title: Food Insecurity and Mortality From Digestive Tract Diseases in the United States.
items.abstract: Food insecurity arising from insufficient access to food necessary for an active and healthy lifestyle is a prevalent yet underrecognized predictor of health that can increase the risk of chronic disorders. The impact of food insecurity on mortality rates from digestive tract diseases within the United States was analyzed. County-level age-standardized mortality rates for digestive tract diseases, encompassing both gastrointestinal tract and liver diseases, were obtained for 2015-2020 and linked to corresponding county-level measures of food insecurity, access to stores, enrollment in food programs, and other local variables. Separate analyses were performed for cancer and for noncancer conditions. Mortality rates from digestive diseases were significantly higher in counties within the highest compared to those with the lowest quintile of food insecurity. These associations remained positive when assessed separately for gastrointestinal tract or liver diseases, or for cancers and noncancer diseases. Food insecurity was associated with mortality from some cancers such as primary liver and colorectal cancers, but not for others such as esophageal or gallbladder cancer. Within food-insecure regions, factors such as younger age, population size and health, health care access, and economic factors were related to higher rates. Composite measures of social vulnerability or deprivation could identify locations with higher mortality. Food insecurity has a significant and detrimental association with mortality rates from digestive tract diseases. These findings emphasize the need to address food access with targeted interventions and for research on disease-specific impacts as crucial determinants of disease-related outcomes.

items.title: CD147+ Cancer-Associated Fibroblasts Promote PD-L1 Expression in Hepatocellular Carcinoma via TIMP2/MMP2/IL-6 Signaling.
items.abstract: Targeting CD147 on hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) cells has demonstrated therapeutic efficacy. Cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) have been identified as critical components of the tumor microenvironment. The role of CD147 in CAFs is still unclear, and this study aims to explore its function. We analyzed single-cell RNA-seq data to identify CD147 expression in CAFs. Flow cytometry and multiplex immunohistochemistry (mIHC) were used to validate protein levels. CD147 function was assessed via shRNA/overexpression. Protein interactions were examined by molecular docking and co-immunoprecipitation (Co-IP). Organoid co-culture system was established to study tumor-immune interactions. Single-cell sequencing and mIHC analyses have confirmed the presence of CD147+CAFs within tumor and adjacent tissues, with tumor-derived CAFs exhibiting elevated CD147 transcript levels. The proportion of CD147+ CAFs varied among patients and demonstrated no significant correlation with CD147 expression in HCC cells. Functionally, CD147+ CAFs secreted higher levels of IL-6 compared to CD147- counterparts. We elucidated a mechanism wherein CD147 on CAFs competitively binds to the tissue inhibitor of metalloproteinase 2 (TIMP2), thereby diminishing TIMP2-mediated inhibition of matrix metalloproteinase 2 (MMP2). Free MMP2 enhances IL-6 secretion via the integrin α5β1 signaling pathway. IL-6 subsequently upregulates PD-L1 expression on HCC cells. This phenomenon was validated both in vitro and organoid co-culture model, where a higher burden of CD147+ CAFs correlated with increased levels of IL-6 and PD-L1. Our study delineates a novel CAF-driven immunosuppressive pathway in HCC, where CD147+ CAFs enhance tumor cell PD-L1 expression and susceptibility to immune checkpoint blockade via a TIMP2/MMP2/IL-6 axis. CD147 has been primarily viewed as a therapeutic marker on HCC cells and has supported the development of CD147-targeted treatment strategies. This study shows that CD147 is also expressed in CAFs and functions as an independent regulator of the immune microenvironment by promoting IL 6 secretion and tumor PD-L1 upregulation. Importantly, CD147 expression in CAFs is not correlated with its expression in tumor cells. These findings suggest that evaluation of CD147 in both tumor and stromal compartments may improve patient stratification and may identify additional patients who could potentially benefit from CD147-targeted or combination immunotherapy approaches.

items.title: Differential Modulation of WNT/β-Catenin Pathway-Associated Molecular Responses by Palmitate and Oleate in Lipid-Loaded HepG2 Cells.
items.abstract: Palmitate (PA) and oleate (OA), the predominant saturated and monounsaturated fatty acids, respectively, may differentially influence hepatic signaling. However, their individual and combined effects on WNT/β-catenin-related responses in HepG2 cells remain incompletely characterized. Human HepG2 cells were exposed to PA, OA, or a combined PA/OA treatment for 24 h. Cell viability was determined via MTT assay, while intracellular lipid droplet (LD) accumulation was evaluated using Oil Red O staining. Transcriptional alterations of canonical WNT/β-catenin cascade genes (WNT, CTNNB1, GSK-3β, TCF, LEF, Axin1, and Axin2) were analyzed by RT-qPCR. Protein expression levels of WNT, β-catenin, and Glypican-3 (GPC3) were evaluated to assess pathway activation. Both fatty acids induced dose-dependent cytotoxicity and intracellular lipid accumulation, with the combined PA/OA treatment provoking the highest LD content. At the molecular level, palmitate predominantly activated the canonical cascade, significantly upregulating WNT, CTNNB1, TCF, and Axin2 mRNA, alongside elevated WNT, β-catenin, and GPC3 protein levels. Conversely, oleate selectively upregulated LEF and GSK-3β without coordinated canonical cascade activation, maintaining lower WNT and GPC3 protein expressions. Interestingly, co-treatment with PA/OA yielded intermediate molecular responses, partially attenuating palmitate-induced activation of WNT and Axin2, and facilitating a partial recovery of Axin1 expression. PA and OA differentially modulated WNT/β-catenin pathway-associated responses in lipid-loaded HepG2 cells. PA elicited a broader response involving WNT, CTNNB1, TCF, Axin2, WNT, and β-catenin, whereas OA produced a more selective response. Their combination partially attenuated PA-associated changes, highlighting fatty acid composition as a potential determinant of cellular responses to lipotoxic stress.
